content: The management of Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) and Hyperglycemic Hyperosmolar State (HHS) requires meticulous monitoring of blood glucose levels. Insulin infusions must be carefully adjusted based on the patient’s current metabolic state to ensure effective treatment. Regular assessment of electrolyte levels is essential to identify and correct any imbalances. Additionally, fluid administration plays a critical role in addressing the elevated osmolarity that is frequently observed in cases of HHS.
